svg.title: How CodeNib searches before repair on ContextBench
svg.desc: An original issue goes to a first Claude Haiku 5.5 search window, which repeatedly chooses glob, grep and read calls from what it has just read, for up to 20 turns. The CodeNib coordinator merges the source ranges it observed and passes navigation of at most 2,048 tokens, locations only and no source, to a complementary Haiku scout window. The scout runs its own search loop to find missed entry points, callers, alternate paths and tests. The coordinator unions both windows' observed ranges, counting overlaps once: this search context reaches 77.07% line recall on 500 tasks. Bounded navigation then goes to a Claude Opus 5.5 repair window, which fetches source through CodeNib tools, edits and self-tests; 388 of 500 tasks are resolved, 77.60% native Pass@1. Adding confirmed repair reads gives 77.90% final line recall. Search costs $0.0114 of model usage per task; repair accounts for 98.32% of model usage. On the official ContextBench Agent systems leaderboard as of 2026-10-23 UTC, the complete agent ranks first in line recall and Pass@1.
svg.text: Search reaches 77% line recall before repair begins.
Full agent #1 · line recall & Pass@1 · 2026-10-23 UTC

Navigation carries locations, not source. Each window reads the code it needs; the coordinator keeps the union of what was observed.
500 ContextBench tasks, scores macro-averaged per task · fixed role routing · glob, grep and reads only: no embeddings, Jev or graph expansion
